newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway sets 4-year plan, sees GDP up 2.75 pct yr/y.
newsitem.headline: Norway sets 4-year plan, sees GDP up 2.75 pct yr/y.

text.p: The Norwegian government said on Friday it expected overall gross domestic product (GDP) to grow by an average 2.75 percent per year to 2001 and by 0.75 percent per annum from 2001 to 2005.
The government, presenting its long-term programme for the period 1998 to 2001, said mainland GDP was forecast to grow by an average annual rate of two percent to 2005.

It projected the yearly rise in consumer prices at 2.5 percent up to 2005, while employment was seen increasing by an average annual rate of one percent to 2001 and by 0.5 percent thereafter up to 2005.
The unemployment rate was forecast to decline to four percent in 2001 from 4.9 percent in 1996.
The minority Labour government said wage inflation was expected to be below or on par with Norway's trading partners.
Oil-rich Norway is one of the few European countries to show a budget surplus, which amounted to 45.7 billion crowns in 1996 and was forecast in the 1997 budget document at 55.4 billion crowns.
This surplus is ploughed into the state's Petroleum Fund for investment overseas.
In its latest plan, the government said the state's net cash flow from petroleum activities was estimated to reach a peak of 10 percent of GDP in 2001, and then gradually decline.
The Petroleum Fund may exceed 400 billion crowns by 2001, it said, based on projections of an average oil price of 115 crowns per barrel. --Oslo newsroom, +47 22 42 50 41
